summary: Big Poe Mountain, Centre County: 1915 tree post, 1920 steel tower demolished by lightning in 1921; an 80 ft steel tower stood by 1958, removed 1993. Site today not described.

facts.design: Four-legged steel tower with a metal cabin (1958 survey); the first structure was a 1915 tree observation post
facts.status_note: The register says it is no longer standing. A June 1921 lightning strike demolished the 1920 steel tower; the Eastern US Lookouts timeline lists its removal in 1993.

events.note: Tree observation post 25 feet above the ground; the register gives 1915 for its tree tower
Steel tower almost complete in May 1920, planned at 60 feet on the Kishacoquillas State Forest
Lightning in a severe storm struck the tower and telephone line; the tower was demolished
National Geodetic Survey note says the 1958 station was probably the same as a Poe Mt. Fire Tower of 1935; a probable link only
National Geodetic Survey station description: four-legged steel tower about 80 feet high with a metal cabin
Registered on the Former Fire Lookout Sites register, September 16, 2008

evidence.supports: The state set up a tree observation post about 25 feet up in 1915
evidence.quote: 1915: A tree observation post established 25 feet above the ground.

evidence.supports: The register dates its tree tower to 1915, used around 1917, no longer standing
evidence.quote: This tree tower was built in 1915 and still used circa 1917. It is no longer standing.

evidence.supports: A September 27, 1919 notice said the State Forestry association had authorized steel observation towers for the forest fire protection service, the first to be erected within eight weeks
evidence.quote: The first of the steel observation towers authorized by the State Forestry association as a part of the forest fire protection service in Pennsylvania will be erected within eight weeks.

evidence.supports: One of the first towers was to go on Big Poe
evidence.quote: One of the first towers will be erected on Big Poe mountain, Coburn township, Centre county.

evidence.supports: The May 1920 notice said the steel tower was almost complete on the Kishacoquillas State Forest
evidence.quote: Forester W.E. Montgomery has almost completed a new steel fire tower on Big Poe Mountain on the Kishacoquillas State Forest.

evidence.supports: The planned height was 60 feet, and a watchman on the platform would see fires over the Seven Mountains district
evidence.quote: When finished, the tower will be sixty feet high. From its platform, a forest fire watchman will be able to detect forest fires on a large area of the State forests in the Seven Mountains district.

evidence.supports: A June 1921 storm, with lightning, demolished the tower and the telephone line
evidence.quote: The telephone line and forest fire observation tower of the Pennsylvania department of forestry on Big Poe mountain, near Milroy, were struck by lightning and demolished during a severe electrical storm on Sunday.

evidence.supports: The observer's cabin was badly wrecked in the storm
evidence.quote: Four telephone poles near the tower were knocked into splinters and the observer's cabin badly wrecked.

evidence.supports: The 1958 station description: four-legged steel structure with a metal cabin
evidence.quote: THE TOWER IS A FOUR LEGGED STEEL STRUCTURE WHICH SUPPORTS A METAL

evidence.supports: The 1958 tower was about 80 feet high
evidence.quote: THE TOWER IS ABOUT 80 FEET HIGH.

evidence.supports: The station was 4 miles southeast of Spring Mills on the highest point of Poe Mountain
evidence.quote: 4.0 MILES SOUTHEAST OF SPRING MILLS AND ON THE HIGHEST POINT OF

evidence.supports: The station description was made by the Coast and Geodetic Survey in 1958
evidence.quote: DESCRIBED BY COAST AND GEODETIC SURVEY 1958 (WER)

evidence.supports: The survey says the station was probably the same as a 1935 Poe Mt. fire tower
evidence.quote: NOTE- THIS STATION IS PROBABLY THE SAME AS POE MT. FIRE TOWER, 1935.

evidence.supports: The Eastern US Lookouts timeline lists the tower as removed in 1993
A DCNR event listing mentions a Watcher's Cabin where a fire tower once stood; it does not name the tower
evidence.quote: as well as the Watcher's Cabin where the fire tower once stood.

sources.title: Big Poe Mountain Tower Site (Centre County)

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A May 1920 notice gives 60 feet for the steel tower as it was being finished; the 1958 survey gives about 80 feet for a four-legged tower. The record keeps 24.4 m from the survey, and the story gives both figures.

notes_for_editor: Almost all of the history comes from one compiled page (Eastern US Lookouts), which quotes newspapers and an NGS datasheet; the NGS text was not checked against NGS directly. The DCNR link to this site is unproven: the listing names no tower or date. Do not merge with the Perry County Big Poe Mountain record (a separate 1909 tree tower on the register). No source states current access, so facts.access is omitted. No photos found.
